items.title: Tom Baker interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997
items.q: And Rolf Harris was on the bill with us, along with Roger Woodward the pianist

ctx.x: When we think of Australian music, we think of novelty songs. Like “Tie Me Kangaroo Down, Sport.”

Well I happened to tour Japan with this multi-instrumentalist, James Morrison. And it was the expo in Tokyo, and every country had a week to do their own thing, present their own music and their food. And Rolf Harris was on the bill with us, along with Roger Woodward the pianist, and opera stars and a few other people. And Rolf did “Tie Me Kangaroo Down,” and he played the wobble board, which was just a board — quite effective. And he did this thing where we played [sings] “Sakura” da da da da da you © Hamilton…

know the Japanese theme. And he set out the front. And he’d do a watercolor, which was real good, and when we finished the tune, he finished the watercolor and signed it, and then proceeded to give it to these people in the front, for charity. And they’d auction it off and they’d get all this money. And he did this on every concert in Japan. He finished with a watercolor, and gave it to charity. So I thought that was a good thing to do.
